topic: The alarm clock that everyone hates every morning.

episode.title: If Things Could Talk: The Alarm Clock

shots.narration: I get slapped every morning for being right.
shots.scene: Cosy modern bedroom at dawn, bright 3D cartoon style, vertical 9:16 frame, no text or numerals.
shots.action: A sleepy human hand presses the top button of a yellow alarm clock with big startled eyes, a tiny flattened mouth, and a blank analog dial.
shots.mood: Warm peach light, exaggerated comic injustice.

shots.narration: Last night, they trusted me with their entire future.
shots.scene: Same bedroom at bedtime, yellow bedside lamp, vertical 9:16 composition, no text or numerals.
shots.action: A human hand adjusts the rear knob of the yellow alarm clock, whose big proud eyes and tiny confident smile sit beneath its blank analog dial.

shots.narration: [excited] Morning arrives, and I deliver my finest performance.
shots.scene: Same bedside table at sunrise, rumpled bed behind it, vertical 9:16 frame, no text or numerals.
shots.action: The yellow alarm clock, with big eager eyes, a tiny open mouth, and a blank analog dial, vibrates on the bedside table.
shots.mood: Bright sunrise colours, enthusiastic theatrical energy.

shots.narration: Apparently, my finest performance needs a snooze button.
shots.scene: Sunlit bedside table beside an occupied rumpled bed, vertical 9:16 frame, no text or numerals.
shots.action: A human finger depresses the yellow alarm clock's top button while its big eyes droop above a tiny disappointed mouth beneath its blank analog dial.

shots.narration: They pull the blanket up like I've been defeated.
shots.scene: Same bedroom, bedside table in foreground and bed behind, vertical 9:16 frame, no text or numerals.
shots.action: The sleeper pulls the duvet over their head beside the yellow alarm clock, whose big narrowed eyes and tiny unimpressed mouth remain visible beneath its blank analog dial.

shots.narration: [sighs] Fine. I'll schedule another deeply unpopular concert.
shots.scene: Same bedside table in stronger morning sunlight, vertical 9:16 frame, no text or numerals.
shots.action: The yellow alarm clock, with big determined eyes, a tiny open mouth, and a blank analog dial, vibrates again.
shots.mood: Cheerful bright light, determined comic persistence.

shots.narration: Now they're late, which is somehow also my fault.
shots.scene: Bedroom with open doorway and discarded slippers, vertical 9:16 frame, no text or numerals.
shots.action: The sleeper rushes through the doorway past the yellow alarm clock, whose big bewildered eyes and tiny round mouth sit beneath its blank analog dial.

shots.narration: Then they greet the coffee mug like a hero.
shots.scene: Breakfast nook adjoining the bedroom, yellow alarm clock visible on the bedside table through the doorway, vertical 9:16 frame, no text or numerals.
shots.action: The person hugs a plain coffee mug while the yellow alarm clock watches with big offended eyes and a tiny downturned mouth beneath its blank analog dial.
shots.mood: Warm kitchen light, absurdly affectionate coffee welcome.

shots.narration: [sarcastic] Tomorrow, ask the mug why its wake-up calls get kisses.
shots.scene: Same breakfast nook with bedroom visible beyond, vertical 9:16 frame, no text or numerals.
shots.action: The person kisses the plain coffee mug beside the doorway framing the yellow alarm clock's big incredulous eyes, tiny scowling mouth, and blank analog dial.

episode.endHook: Next episode: the coffee mug explains who really carries mornings.
episode.description: An alarm clock shares its side of everyone's least favorite morning routine. It does its job perfectly—and still gets slapped for it.
